method: Real disposable production TLS app; actual authenticated fixture ingest and shipped UI, original PNGs, no response/DOM substitutions or postcapture image edits.
publication_scope: Approved by the owner on 2026-11-21 for the public repository README/docs/assets, with synthetic-data captions; not a claim of scanner or model accuracy.
scope_limits: Synthetic fixture observations and leases; no attached radio, physical scan or model-accuracy claim.
No Grafana UI is deployed; the application metrics endpoint is actual runtime data.
Protocol Summary groups require fresh scanner leases; this fixture enables only SDR and Wi-Fi, with System always visible.

SDR Active Freqs is the server count of positive raw frequencies in 100 kHz bins over the fixed last hour, independent of the bounded recent feed. Summary detection total/rate use their existing 24-hour window; other Summary metrics retain their own scopes.
The Wi-Fi anomaly tile matches the current default active anomaly queue, including a verified zero. It is not a count of all retained anomaly history.
SDR views fully show KPIs, timeline and class distribution; the lower heatmap continues below the viewport.
Historical RF graphs come from submitted timestamps; Wi-Fi observation times are actual ingest times.
Browser accepts the disposable self-signed TLS certificate; the API client verifies the matching CA.
The visible Connected indicator means at least one dashboard WebSocket is open; it does not establish physical scanner readiness.

screenshots.caption: Fourteen bands of labeled synthetic RF observations, with actual stored counts and mean received power. Frequency labels do not prove protocol identity.
Actual API aggregates for the synthetic RF/Wi-Fi fixture. The rate is the application's window average, not a physical receiver throughput benchmark.
Real timeline, class distribution and fixed last-hour active-frequency count from timestamped synthetic detections; no chart or response substitution.
Eight synthetic networks and twenty-four locally administered client identities across three bands; no nearby private network data.
Alerts created by the actual condition-rule engine from labeled synthetic RF input; no outbound webhook is configured.
The real known-RF review flow, scoped to one synthetic node and frequency interval; stored detections remain intact.
The shipped checklist distinguishes synthetic capture reports and stored observations from unreported physical host readiness.
Accessible contextual help on the live, populated dashboard; text is shipped product copy.
